implement

/IM-pluh-ment/ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To implement is to put something into effect.

The principal decided to implement a new dress code next fall.

Example

For a year, the city council's recycling proposal existed only as a document in a binder. Then crews began delivering blue bins to every home, new truck routes were scheduled, and the sorting facility opened its doors.

The moment the plan stopped being words on paper and became real action is the moment it was implemented. Implement is more precise than 'start' or 'do' because it specifically means carrying out a plan or policy that was already designed.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

execute: To execute is to carry out a specific plan, order, or move, focusing on performing the steps — a pilot executes a landing. To implement is to take a designed plan or policy and set it working in the real world; you implement the program, then execute each step it calls for.

enact: To enact is to make something official policy or law — the vote passes, the signature lands, the rule is on the books. Implementing comes next: a council enacts a recycling law on paper, but the city implements it only when bins are delivered and routes actually run.

apply: To apply is to put something to practical use in one particular case — you apply a rule to a single essay or a technique to one problem. To implement is larger in scale: it means putting a whole plan or system into effect so it operates day to day.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

abandon: give up a plan completely

shelve: set a plan aside indefinitely

Where it sits · how far from idea into action — propose → adopt → implement → enforce

propose vs. implement: Propose is much weaker than implement — proposing a plan only suggests it, while implementing a plan actually puts it into action.

adopt vs. implement: Adopt is weaker than implement; a school that adopts a policy has officially accepted it, but to implement it means making it work day to day.

enforce vs. implement: Enforce is stronger than implement — to implement a rule sets it in motion, while enforcing it means actively making sure everyone follows it.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — im-

prefix — im-: in, into (Latin)

root — ple

root — ple: to fill (Latin (plere))

suffix — -ment

suffix — -ment: result or means of an action (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Im- (in) + ple (fill) + -ment (means of): literally 'a filling in.' To implement a plan is to fill in what was promised — to carry it fully into effect.

Use the root in a new word: complete

Use the root in a new word: complete: She needed just one more credit to complete her diploma.
